why `custom` ? libspdm uses `cmake` build system right ?
Yes, I tried that but was not working before - giving some ninja install issues - hence moved to custom, I trired again and it worked.
Mrking as Resolved

should not really need these. CMake support -S and -B options to capture the source as well as build directories.

```
  -S <path-to-source>          = Explicitly specify a source directory.
  -B <path-to-build>           = Explicitly specify a build directory.
```

so you can actually do 

```
cmake -S . -B build <options>
```
If we are using the build type as cmake we don't need to pass this and we don't need the above highlighted steps.
Marking as Resolved

it's weird that we need to provide the ARCH even for native builds, ARCH probably is meant for cross compilation.

But this would break, if the docker is run on x86 servers. So at least we should pick the arch from `uname -m` rather than hard-coding this.

Pushed https://github.com/DMTF/libspdm/pull/3148 to add auto-detection of ARCH in libspdm. please feel free to leave a review if you are convinced.
I have added the script to get the arch dynamically from the machine.
Mraking as Resolved

Also, If I give the DTOOLCHAIN=NONE, It doesn't work, It asks for the libopenssl lib.
DMTF/libspdm: /usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lopenssllib: No such file or directory

openssllib is supplied through the os_stub inside libspdm but it should not be having any dependency while it builds libspdm_crypto.so

DMTF/libspdm: : && /usr/bin/cc -fPIC -Os   -shared -Wl,-soname,libspdm_crypto.so -o lib/libspdm_crypto.so .......-lopenssllib  lib/libcryptlib_openssl.a &&
Marking as Resolved.
cannot seem to figure out if this was a configurable option, can you please point where this is defined ?

I got it from here https://github.com/openbmc/openbmc/blob/master/meta-openembedded/meta-oe/recipes-support/libspdm/libspdm_3.6.0.bb

But when I read the Cmakelist inside libspdm 3.6.0, I find this which suggest that if binary build is enabled then they disabling the EDDSA

    # Disable EDDSA when binary builds are enabled. EDDSA may be enabled in the future.
    add_definitions(-DLIBSPDM_EDDSA_ED25519_SUPPORT=0)
    add_definitions(-DLIBSPDM_EDDSA_ED448_SUPPORT=0)

    message("ENABLE_BINARY_BUILD=1")
    message("COMPILED_LIBCRYPTO_PATH=${COMPILED_LIBCRYPTO_PATH}")
    message("COMPILED_LIBSSL_PATH=${COMPILED_LIBSSL_PATH}")
    message("Disabling EDDSA support due to ENABLE_BINARY_BUILD=1")


Hence removing it.

wouldn't this automatically happen when we defined the `build_type` as `cmake` ?
Nopes, These are the necessary options.
Marking as Resolved

why do we need all of this ? by default if we define build_type as cmake, it would automatically build & install things 
```
 def _cmd_build_cmake(self) -> str:
        options = " ".join(self.pkg_def.get("config_flags", []))
        env = " ".join(self.pkg_def.get("config_env", []))
        result = "mkdir builddir && cd builddir && "
        result += f"{env} cmake {cmake_flags} {options} .. && "
        result += "cmake --build . --target all && "
        result += "cmake --build . --target install && "
        result += "cd .."
```

Look at the cmake support at https://github.com/openbmc/openbmc-build-scripts/blob/master/scripts/build-unit-test-docker#L626
I responded above.
